Metadata.CommitMsg: chore: high/critical vulnerabilities detected in gosec
Metadata.Author: hsri-pf9 <hsri-pf9@users.noreply.github.com>

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent: in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh/agent
Vulnerabilities.Description: SSH Agent servers do not validate the size of messages when processing new identity requests, which may cause the program to panic if the message is malformed due to an out of bounds read.

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang.org/x/crypto/ssh: in golang.org/x/crypto/ssh
Vulnerabilities.Description: SSH servers parsing GSSAPI authentication requests do not validate the number of mechanisms specified in the request, allowing an attacker to cause unbounded memory consumption.

Vulnerabilities.Title: golang.org/x/oauth2/jws: Unexpected memory consumption during token parsing in golang.org/x/oauth2/jws
Vulnerabilities.Description: An attacker can pass a malicious malformed token which causes unexpected memory to be consumed during parsing.

Vulnerabilities.Title: jose-go: improper handling of highly compressed data
Vulnerabilities.Description: Package jose aims to provide an implementation of the Javascript Object Signing and Encryption set of standards. An attacker could send a JWE containing compressed data that used large amounts of memory and CPU when decompressed by Decrypt or DecryptMulti. Those functions now return an error if the decompressed data would exceed 250kB or 10x the compressed size (whichever is larger). This vulnerability has been patched in versions 4.0.1, 3.0.3 and 2.6.3.
